H&P – Super Detailed

Consult Summary:
45-year-old man with 5-day history of dry cough, rhinorrhea, myalgias, headache, and chills; no dyspnea or wheeze; exam shows mild pharyngeal erythema—assessment: viral upper respiratory tract infection; advised symptomatic OTC therapy and return precautions.

History:
• Presenting complaint: “cough and cold.”  
• Onset: Began ~5 days ago (start of last weekend).  
• Course: Persistent but not worsening; no improvement yet reported.  
• Character: Dry, hacking cough; clear nasal discharge; generalized muscle aches; occasional headache; chills.  
• Associated symptoms: Denies hemoptysis, dyspnea, wheeze, or chest tightness. No reported fever measurement.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: Uses paracetamol with some relief; has not used ibuprofen.  
• Review of systems (pertinent negatives): No sore throat beyond mild irritation noted on exam; no neck gland tenderness; no gastrointestinal, urinary, or neurological complaints mentioned.

Past Medical History:
• Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus – diagnosed 5–6 years ago; home glucose monitoring “within normal range.”  
  – Medication: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Hypertension – “slight blood pressure problem;” last home BP reading today “within normal range.”  
  – Medication: Lisinopril (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Social History:
• No details regarding occupation, living situation, smoking, alcohol, or recreational drug use documented.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
• General: Not directly observed; patient conversant and not in respiratory distress via video.  
• HEENT: Mild erythema of posterior pharynx; tonsils not enlarged. No cervical lymphadenopathy reported by patient.  
• Chest/Lungs: No wheeze, rattles, or shortness of breath reported; no auscultation data available.  
• Vitals: Not provided.

Investigations:
• None performed or reviewed.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Viral upper respiratory tract infection (common cold)
  • Assessment based on 5-day history of dry cough, rhinorrhea, systemic aches, normal respiratory status, and benign throat exam.
  • Plan:
    – Symptomatic relief with OTC preparations (Day Nurse/Night Nurse) compatible with current medications.
    – Continue paracetamol as needed.
    – Adequate hydration and rest.
    – Return precautions: seek medical care if develops shortness of breath, wheeze, hemoptysis, fever, or if symptoms persist >3 weeks.
    – No antibiotics or additional prescriptions at this time.

General plan items:
• Continue regular medications (metformin, lisinopril).
• Monitor blood glucose and blood pressure as usual.

• Current medication doses, routes, frequencies not documented.
• Smoking, alcohol, and other social history absent.
• No vital signs recorded.
